scope: All numbers come from the enumerable synthetic control environment of data/controlled.py (Z_97, 4 non-commuting affine experts, 84 terminal paths at budget 3). They compare training signals for one small linear router policy and verify estimator properties (unbiasedness, variance, budget semantics). They are not evidence about natural-language models, and no language-model RL was performed.

real_lm_rl.reason: The E09 real-LM router-RL part (frozen backbone, Top-2 set actions, teacher-forced terminal reward) requires the training stack and is outside this script; only the enumerable synthetic analogue runs here.

environment.policy: shared linear factorized STOP/expert policy, weights (5, 12), deployment-legal observations only

gradient_verification.note: reinforce_b0, reinforce_mean_baseline and rloo2_loo are unbiased (bias ~1e-16); self_mean_g2 includes the sample in its own baseline, is biased toward grad/2, and its low variance must not be read as an advantage.

cost.note: Optimal-path labels are computed once by full enumeration; each update then costs zero rollouts.

budget.note: env.step raises on any illegal decision and the forced exit at min(budget, MAX_CALLS) carries probability 1, so a hard violation cannot be sampled; every rollout above asserted 1 <= calls <= limit. Overspend = expected calls under the trained policy minus the optimal path length.

findings: Supervised imitation of the enumerable optimal paths recovers 6/6 designed optima at ~zero per-update rollout cost (final batch objective 0.1832); exact joint score-function descent reaches a lower batch objective (0.1510) yet recovers only 4/6 designed optima — the joint objective is non-convex in the router weights, and batch E[F] and greedy path recovery are different criteria.

On-policy G=2 RLOO has exactly the same expected update as exact descent (enumeration identity err 5.13e-16) plus batch total gradient variance 0.0590 at init (vs 0.2958 for unbaselined REINFORCE); across seeds its final batch objective is 0.2771 ± 0.0713 (range [0.1610, 0.3356]), and its best seed recovers 1/6 designed optima — the sampled estimator inherits the exact update's local optima and adds cross-seed variance on top.

Held-out recovery on fresh random instances is modest for every method (supervised 0.250): one linear policy trained on 6 tasks generalizes weakly, so none of the designed-set gains should be read as general competence.
All conclusions are restricted to this enumerable synthetic environment; nothing here licenses or refutes router RL on a real language model (that part of E09 is marked not_executed).
